pack.title: “So what do you do?”
pack.description: The verdict disguised as a question. Answer it once, then ask better.

scenarios.setting: Wedding reception. A stranger asks it like a verdict, drink in hand.

replies.line: I'd rather start with how we know the couple.
replies.why: It suggests another basis for connection without inventing a profession.
replies.delivery: Answer with your real work if you want; ask the next question with genuine curiosity.

replies.line: How do you know the couple?
replies.why: It redirects toward the event rather than a status comparison.
replies.delivery: Answer with your real work if you want; ask the next question with genuine curiosity.

replies.line: Happy to chat, but first, how do you know the couple?
replies.why: It welcomes conversation while choosing a less evaluative opening.
replies.delivery: Answer with your real work if you want; ask the next question with genuine curiosity.

replies.line: Currently? Professional cake taster. Unpaid, but I'm committed.
replies.why: An absurd job title answers the ritual while refusing the ranking.
replies.delivery: Answer with your real work if you want; ask the next question with genuine curiosity.

trap.line: I do pretty well, actually. Very well.
trap.why: It replaces a specific request with accusation, resentment, or an excuse, making your actual boundary less clear.

scenarios.goal: Keep an introduction from becoming a status test.

followUp.jab: No, what do you actually do for work?
followUp.line: I can tell you a little; I'd rather this not be a job interview.
followUp.why: It sets a conversational limit without inventing a profession.
followUp.delivery: Answer with your real work if you want; ask the next question with genuine curiosity.

scenarios.setting: Networking event. Name tags, bad wine, worse questions.
scenarios.jab: What do you do? And be honest — is it actually interesting?

replies.line: I enjoy parts of it. What interests you outside work?
replies.why: It answers honestly without accepting an audition for impressiveness.
replies.delivery: Pause, then say “I enjoy parts of it” at a steady, conversational volume. Ask the next question as an invitation rather than a counterattack.

replies.why: It declines a detailed work discussion and returns the question.
replies.delivery: Say “Boring stuff” clearly, then stop instead of adding a defense. Ask the next question as an invitation rather than a counterattack.

replies.line: Honestly? Some days. Tell me the interesting version of your job.
replies.why: It gives a measured answer and invites the other person to describe their interests.
replies.delivery: Keep “Honestly” warm and unhurried; finish the request clearly. Ask the next question as an invitation rather than a counterattack.

replies.line: I make small talk at networking events. Living the dream.
replies.why: It jokes about the present interaction instead of inventing a career.
replies.delivery: Keep “I make small talk at networking events” light; let the joke stand without repeating it. Ask the next question as an invitation rather than a counterattack.

scenarios.goal: Share your work without accepting a dismissive evaluation.

followUp.line: It suits me. What do you enjoy outside work?
followUp.why: It declines the ranking and offers a different basis for connection.
followUp.delivery: Keep “suits me” relaxed; ask the next question as an invitation rather than a counterattack.

scenarios.setting: Dinner party. You say you're between jobs; the table goes quiet.
scenarios.jab: Oh. So what do you… do all day?

replies.line: I'm between jobs. I'd rather talk about something else.
replies.why: It gives only the information you choose and sets a topic boundary.
replies.delivery: Keep your tone ordinary; you do not need to describe a happy job search if that is untrue.

replies.line: I'm figuring out what's next; I'd enjoy hearing about something besides work tonight.
replies.why: It stays honest about uncertainty while offering a different conversation.
replies.delivery: Keep your tone ordinary; you do not need to describe a happy job search if that is untrue.

replies.why: The joke lightly names the repeated questions without revealing private information.
replies.delivery: Keep your tone ordinary; you do not need to describe a happy job search if that is untrue.

replies.line: I'd rather not discuss my job search.
replies.why: It states the immediate boundary without adding a personal judgment.
replies.delivery: Keep your tone ordinary; you do not need to describe a happy job search if that is untrue.

trap.line: Well at least I'm not defined by my job like some people.
trap.why: It replaces a specific request with accusation, resentment, or an excuse, making your actual boundary less clear.

scenarios.goal: Protect your privacy while between jobs.

followUp.jab: But how are you paying for things?
followUp.line: I'm keeping the financial details private; let's talk about something else.
followUp.why: It sets a clear limit on a more personal follow-up.
followUp.delivery: Keep your tone ordinary; you do not need to describe a happy job search if that is untrue.
